title: Transactional systems versus analytical systems
summary: Start from the question and workload, not the database logo.

claims.text: OLAP serves analytical exploration and aggregation rather than the short transactional operations that motivate OLTP.

levels.overview: Explain an order being recorded versus an analyst studying orders over time.
levels.architecture: Show operational inputs, integration, analytic model and consumer separately. A logical role need not be a separate deployed service.
levels.detail: Ask about concurrent writes, consistency, row grain, query shape, retention and refresh boundaries.

example.input: Two fictional orders and a request for monthly sales.
steps: Group the retained sales by month.
example.output: A transaction path and an analysis path with different responsibilities.
limits: No throughput, cost or latency result is supplied.

alternatives.label: Single-store reporting
alternatives.whenToConsider: Small selected workloads may justify avoiding another store.

alternatives.label: Separate analytical serving
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when workload or historical requirements justify separation.

interview.question: Why is a transactional schema not automatically the best reporting model?
answerHints: Avoid claiming one physical design fits every case.

instanceMappingPolicy: An explicit source-pinned link is required; names, icons and tags are not evidence.
